comments.text: > pop music lacks musicality, most of what they listed were to do with sonic tricks that are not really tied to musicality or musicianship This is a paradox, though. You’re saying that one of the most popular types of music “lacks musicality”. The only way that can be true is if you start with a narrow and arbitrary definition of what “musicality” is. If you examine the history of ideas of what is “real” or “authentic” or “objectively good” in music, who has been a proponent of those ideas through history, and why, you will find is that a lot of it is rooted in white supremacy. The idea is that a certain style of white European music is the only true music, and that other music is only valuable to the extent that it happens to fit within the theoretical frameworks developed around those styles. I guess what I’m saying is, please watch this excellent video, “Music Theory is Racist” by Adam Neely: [VIDEO]

comments.author: shirleyquirk

comments.why_zh: 对乐理的政治性批评给出了清晰、有趣且带有怀疑态度的解读。
comments.quote_zh: 我推荐 YouTube 上的 Adam Neely
comments.text_zh: 我在一个古典音乐家家庭长大，拿了音乐学位，自己也短暂当过职业古典音乐家。所以我的建议可能和第一次学音乐的人的体验很不搭，但我学习欧洲古典乐理之外的内容的经历，让我觉得受到了侮辱。乐理的基础被呈现得好像它们是一切后续音乐由之衍生的根基。事实上，教音阶和和弦就像教“电子绕着原子核转”——一种“简化”。确实存在真正的心理声学事实，也存在同样迷人的历史力量，它们共同支撑着乐理。尽管去学乐理的语言和惯用法，但千万别以为它在任何意义上都是“真理”。它是一场混合主义的货物崇拜，由几个世纪以来动机可疑的男人们传下来的一堆凑合办法和经验法则。我推荐 YouTube 上的 Adam Neely，他讲解乐理概念清晰、有趣，并且对既有的智慧保持着恰当的怀疑。这是他讨论对乐理的一些更具政治性批评的视频：[VIDEO]。我向任何对“为什么某些音放在一起好听、另一些不好听”的底层原因感兴趣的人推荐 Sethares 的《Tuning, Timbre, Spectrum, Scale》。[2] [LINK]
comments.text: I grew up in a family of classical musicians, got a degree in music, and was briefly a professional classical musician myself. So my advice may be very out of touch with the experience of someone learning for the first time, but my experiences learning beyond European classical music theory left me feeling insulted. The basics of music theory are presented as though they are the foundations upon which all subsequent music is derived. In fact, teaching scales and chords is like teaching that the electron orbits the nucleus - a 'simplification'. There _are_ real psychoacoustic truths, alongside equally fascinating historical forces, that underpin music theory. Learn the language and idioms of music theory, by all means, but don't think of it as being in any way true. Its a syncretist cargo cult of hacks and rules of thumb handed down by centuries of men with dubious motives. I recommend Adam Neely on YouTube, he illustrates music theory concepts clearly, engagingly, and with an appropriate skepticism for received wisdom. Here's his discussion of some more political criticisms of music theory: [VIDEO] I recommend Sethares' _Tuning, Timbre, Spectrum, Scale_ to anyone interested in the underpinnings of why some notes sound good together and others don't. [2] [LINK]

One example in the video is ragas: they can look a lot like Western scales and modes, but they have a time and context. Western music also has a time and context, but it doesn't stand out as much to us unless someone goes full ham breaking that context like with the Imperial March in a Major mode: [LINK] It changes the mood from "this is the bad guys!" to something more positive and triumphant.

More a collection of rules and conventions used in Western music. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 这些复原听起来西方味浓得离谱。中东有很长一段不使用欧洲十二平均律音阶的历史，幻想它在当下常见语境里会是什么样，确实有点意思，但这么做似乎有点洗白、有点不诚实。比如你可以在这里了解更多：[VIDEO]
comments.text: The recreations are absurdly western sounding. The middle east has a long history of not using 12-tone equal temperament scales of Europe and while it's somewhat interesting to fantasize what it would sound like in the common current context, it seems a little white-washing and disingenuous. You can get more info here for example: [VIDEO]
